title: Fortuny Watercolor Study
content: Mariano Fortuny's father and mother had died by the time he was 12, so he was raised by his grandfather, a craftsman who showed the boy how to make wax figurines. He took his grandson on the road from town to town, presenting the figures they sculpted.Watercolor study by Mariano (or Marià) Fortuny (1838-1874)Young Mariano showed early promise in drawing and painting. In Paris, hestudied withwas inspired by Ernest Meissonier and Jean Leon Gérôme, both of whom made careful studies from costumed models with watercolor.Fortuny died young, but his influence was felt by many younger artists, who carried on his tradition of traveling and adventuring, painting people in exotic costumes.Please see the additional biographical detail provided by Ramon in the comments.----Source:Charles Yriarte, Fortuny (Artistes célèbres series) (Paris, 1886)Book:Fortuny (1838-1874) (Catálago Esposición)
